content.user_title: Explain Code Clearly for Any Audience
content.value_statement: Complex code slows onboarding and reviews. This skill turns code into audience-aware explanations, walkthroughs, diagrams, and practice prompts.
actual_capabilities: Breaks code into purpose, responsibilities, dependencies, and execution flow.
Adapts explanations for junior, mid-level, senior, and non-technical audiences.
Formats walkthroughs with summaries, step-by-step notes, diagrams, and gotchas.
Highlights security, performance, testing, and scalability considerations.
Creates practice exercises and review questions for learning sessions.
limitations: It depends on the user-provided code and context.
It cannot verify runtime behavior unless supporting tests or logs are provided.
It may need project conventions to explain architecture accurately.
It does not replace formal security or performance review.

use_cases.title: Onboard New Developers
use_cases.description: Create plain-language walkthroughs that explain purpose, flow, and common mistakes in unfamiliar code.

use_cases.title: Prepare Code Reviews
use_cases.description: Summarize design choices, dependencies, risks, and testing concerns before a team review.

use_cases.title: Document Complex Services
use_cases.description: Turn service logic into structured documentation with diagrams, examples, and maintenance notes.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Walkthrough
prompt_templates.scenario: A junior developer needs a first explanation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this code for a junior developer. Cover purpose, inputs, outputs, and each step. Avoid unexplained jargon. Code: [paste code]

prompt_templates.title: Team Review Summary
prompt_templates.scenario: A reviewer needs concise context before discussion.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a walkthrough for [file or function]. Include data flow, dependencies, edge cases, and common mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture Explanation
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the architecture behind [module]. Compare design trade-offs, scalability concerns, and testing strategy for senior engineers.

prompt_templates.title: Onboarding Lesson
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs reusable learning material.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this code into onboarding material with a summary, diagram description, exercises, and review questions for [audience].

output_examples.input: A payment service with order lookup, charge creation, status updates, and confirmation email.
output: Overview: The service validates an order, charges the payment method, records success, and sends a receipt.
Key risks: Duplicate charges, client-controlled amounts, and email failures need explicit handling.
Learning prompt: Ask the reader where retry logic should live.

output_examples.input: An authentication middleware chain for protected routes.
output: Flow: Logging runs first, authentication verifies identity, authorization checks access, then the route handles the request.
Common mistake: Running authorization before authentication leaves the user context unavailable.
Diagram suggestion: Show each middleware as a checkpoint in request order.

output_examples.input: A function that fetches records asynchronously and returns a list.
output: Issue explained: The function may return before asynchronous work finishes.
Fix direction: Use a collection method that waits for all requested records.
Audience note: For beginners, explain promises before discussing concurrency.

best_practices: State the audience and knowledge level before asking for an explanation.
Provide related files, tests, and error messages when behavior depends on context.
Ask for diagrams or exercises when the goal is onboarding.
anti_patterns: Do not request one explanation for every audience at once unless comparison is needed.
Do not omit security-sensitive context when explaining authentication or payment code.
Do not treat generated explanations as proof that the code is correct.

faq.question: Can this skill explain unfamiliar languages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can explain many languages when code and context are provided.

faq.question: Does it run my code?
faq.answer: No. It explains provided code and context. Execution depends on the host tool and user permission.

faq.question: Can it help junior developers?
faq.answer: Yes. It can reduce jargon and explain each step in beginner-friendly terms.

faq.question: Can it create diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It can describe or format diagrams for flows, architecture, and state changes.

faq.question: Does it find bugs?
faq.answer: It can point out possible issues, but dedicated tests and reviews are still required.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
